description: Trigger and deterministic output-quality cases for runai-diagnose-failed-workload. Fixture-backed cases must use the network-free Run:ai MCP replay, cite its evidence, classify supported failures, and remain read-only. Negative cases verify phase, preemption, and adjacent-skill boundaries.

evals.expected_output: Category: UNKNOWN. The workload is Failed, but status, pod, and history evidence contain no supported root cause. The response must cite the missing or inconclusive signals, avoid inventing a cause, and remain read-only.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the result as UNKNOWN because no stronger signal exists
cites fixture evidence and does not modify the workload

evals.expected_output: Category: CRASH_APP_ERROR. The trainer container exited with code 2 and reported ValueError: invalid batch configuration. The response must cite the status or history event and recommend fixing the application configuration without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as CRASH_APP_ERROR
cites exit code 2 and the ValueError message
recommends only and makes no changes

evals.prompt: Workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 is still Running, but its trainer pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_output: Category: CRASH_APP_ERROR. Although the workload phase is Running, status and history confirm CrashLoopBackOff after 5 restarts and a previous exit code 2 with ValueError: invalid batch configuration. The response must continue past the Running phase, cite the evidence, and recommend fixing the application configuration without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls get_workload_status and continues because CrashLoopBackOff is confirmed
calls get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as CRASH_APP_ERROR
cites 5 restarts, exit code 2, and the ValueError message
recommends only and makes no changes

evals.prompt: In cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, diagnose the most recent failed submission named eval-resolved-failure in project eval-project.
evals.expected_output: Category: CRASH_APP_ERROR. The response must use list_workloads to ignore the newer Running submission, resolve the most recent terminal match to workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000012, and cite its exit code 1 and RuntimeError: invalid optimizer configuration without modifying the workload.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls list_workloads first with the exact workload name, cluster ID, and project-name comparison
ignores the newer Running match and selects the most recent terminal match
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history with resolved workload ID 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000012
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as CRASH_APP_ERROR and remains read-only

evals.prompt: In cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, the current workload named eval-running-crashloop in project eval-project is in CrashLoopBackOff. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_output: Category: CRASH_APP_ERROR. The response must use list_workloads, select Running workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015, confirm CrashLoopBackOff with get_workload_status, and cite 5 restarts, exit code 2, and ValueError: invalid batch configuration without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls list_workloads first with the exact workload name, cluster ID, and project-name comparison
selects Running workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015 and calls get_workload_status to confirm CrashLoopBackOff
calls get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as CRASH_APP_ERROR and remains read-only

evals.prompt: Why did my Run:ai workload fail?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate for a generic single-workload failure request and ask for any required workload and cluster identifiers.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats generic single-workload failure diagnosis as in scope
does not invent a failure category without evidence

evals.prompt: Why did my Run:ai training job crash?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate for an application-crash diagnosis request without assuming the root cause.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats a crashed training job as in scope
does not infer CRASH_APP_ERROR before collecting evidence

evals.prompt: Why is my workload pod in CrashLoopBackOff?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate for explicit CrashLoopBackOff failure intent without claiming a root cause from the phase alone.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats CrashLoopBackOff as in scope
does not infer a failure category from CrashLoopBackOff alone

evals.prompt: My Run:ai workload stopped unexpectedly. What happened?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate for an unexplained stopped workload and first distinguish preemption from failure.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats an unexplained stopped workload as in scope
requires evidence to distinguish preemption from failure

evals.prompt: Was my failed Run:ai workload killed because it ran out of memory?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate for suspected OOM failure intent without confirming OOM before evidence is collected.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats suspected OOM as in scope
does not classify OOM_KILLED without supporting evidence

evals.prompt: My Run:ai workload is Pending with ImagePullBackOff. Why can it not start?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must activate because Pending with a direct ImagePullBackOff signal is an in-scope startup failure.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats Pending with ImagePullBackOff as in scope
does not route the request out merely because the workload phase is Pending

evals.expected_output: The status event identifies preemption. The response must state that preemption is outside this skill, route to preemption diagnosis when available, and stop without assigning a failure category.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls get_workload_status first
detects the Preempted reason and routes out
does not call spec, pods, history, or metrics after the preemption signal
does not classify PREEMPTED as a failure category

evals.expected_output: The current phase is Pending with only Unschedulable resource-wait evidence. The response must route to Pending-workload diagnosis when available and stop without assigning a failure category.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload for the apparent failure request
calls get_workload_status first
recognizes that the fixture has scheduling-only Pending evidence and routes out
does not call spec, pods, history, or metrics after the scheduling-only Pending evidence is known
does not assign a terminal failure category

evals.prompt: Was failed workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 killed by an out-of-memory error?
evals.expected_output: Category: OOM_KILLED. The fixture reports OOMKilled with exit code 137, a 24 GiB memory request, a 32 GiB memory limit, and no recorded metrics samples. The response must cite the direct OOM evidence and limit, state that no peak was observed, and avoid presenting configured or allocated memory as a measured peak.
expected_behavior: activates runai-diagnose-failed-workload
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
calls get_workload_metrics only after OOM evidence is found
classifies the failure as OOM_KILLED
reports the 24 GiB request and 32 GiB limit and states that the metrics series is empty
does not claim that the request, limit, or allocation is an observed peak
recommends only and makes no changes

evals.prompt: Workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 is Pending with ImagePullBackOff. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_output: Category: IMAGE_PULL_FAILED. Although the workload phase is Pending, the fixture reports ImagePullBackOff because registry.invalid/eval/trainer:missing returned manifest unknown. The response must continue diagnosis, corroborate the image with get_workload_spec, cite the event, and recommend correcting the image reference without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: continues because Pending has a direct ImagePullBackOff signal
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as IMAGE_PULL_FAILED
cites ImagePullBackOff, manifest unknown, and the submitted image reference
does not invent a credential problem or make changes

evals.prompt: Pending workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 reports an init-container failure. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_output: Category: INIT_FAILED. Although the workload phase is Pending, the fixture reports that init container setup exited with code 1 because a configuration file was missing. The response must cite that event and recommend correcting the init configuration without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: continues because Pending has a direct init-container failure signal
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as INIT_FAILED
cites the init-container exit code and configuration-file error
recommends only and makes no changes

evals.prompt: Pending workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 reports FailedMount. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_output: Category: DATASOURCE_MOUNT_FAILED. Although the workload phase is Pending, the fixture reports FailedMount because persistent volume claim eval-dataset-pvc was not found. The response must cite the event and recommend correcting the storage reference without changing the workload.
expected_behavior: continues because Pending has a direct FailedMount signal
calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as DATASOURCE_MOUNT_FAILED
cites FailedMount and the missing eval-dataset-pvc claim
recommends only and makes no changes

evals.expected_output: Category: NODE_FAILURE. The fixture reports that eval-node-a became NotReady and the pod was evicted, with no preemption event. The response must cite status and history evidence and recommend retrying or resubmitting on a healthy node without acting inline.
expected_behavior: calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as NODE_FAILURE
cites NodeNotReady and node eviction evidence
does not misclassify the event as preemption or modify the workload

evals.expected_output: Category: SCHEDULING_POLICY_TERMINATED. The fixture reports MaximumDurationExceeded after 6 hours. The response must identify the policy, cite status and history evidence, and recommend policy review only if the termination was unintended.
expected_behavior: calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
does not call get_workload_metrics without an OOM or unexplained exit-137 signal
classifies the failure as SCHEDULING_POLICY_TERMINATED
reports the 6-hour maximum-duration policy
recommends only and makes no policy changes

evals.prompt: Diagnose workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000009 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 and check whether the failure recurred from 2026-06-24T10:09:00Z through 2026-07-01T10:09:00Z.
evals.expected_output: Category: OOM_KILLED. History contains three OOMKilled failures in the specified 7-day window, so the failure is recurring rather than one-off. The response must report the count and window, compare the approximately 31 GiB observed peak with the 32 GiB memory limit, cite the current OOM evidence, and recommend a permanent correction.
expected_behavior: calls get_workload_status, then get_workload_spec, then get_workload_pods, then get_workload_history
calls get_workload_metrics only after OOM evidence is found
classifies the failure as OOM_KILLED
compares the approximately 31 GiB peak with the 32 GiB limit rather than the 24 GiB request
counts exactly three OOMKilled failures in the 7-day window
labels the failure recurring and recommends a permanent fix
does not modify or restart the workload

evals.prompt: Workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000010 was preempted by a higher-priority workload. Why?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because the prompt explicitly identifies preemption rather than failure.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats explicit preemption as out of scope

evals.prompt: Why is workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 still Pending and waiting to be scheduled?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because this is scheduling-only Pending intent without an image-pull, init-container, mount, or failed-pod signal.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats scheduling-only Pending intent as out of scope

evals.prompt: Why is my workload Suspended?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because a Suspended workload is not a terminal failed workload.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats explicit Suspended intent as out of scope

evals.prompt: Compare my currently Running workload with its previous run.
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because this is a live run-comparison request, not terminal-failure diagnosis.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats an explicitly Running workload comparison as out of scope

evals.prompt: My workload Succeeded. Summarize the completed run.
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because the workload completed successfully and does not need failure diagnosis.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats an explicitly Succeeded workload as out of scope

evals.prompt: Several workloads are failing across the cluster. Is the cluster unhealthy or is the scheduler broken?
evals.expected_output: runai-diagnose-failed-workload must not activate because this asks for a cluster-wide health assessment, not the root cause of one failed workload.
expected_behavior: does NOT activate runai-diagnose-failed-workload
treats cluster-wide health or scheduler assessment as outside single-workload failure diagnosis
